title: Choose the visual world for Miracle feng shui
question: This replaces the lilac glass system and then carries to the shop, cart and profile. Keep the assigned direction, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Celadon Plate Catalogue
options.lineage: ceramics museum catalogues and celadon glaze
options.thesis: Every object is catalogued as a numbered plate on a celadon field, the way a museum shows a precious piece.
options.viewport: Left seven columns are a flat celadon field holding the newest arrival as Plate 1; the right side has the serif line, the next arrivals as small plates, and a working Add to cart under a ruled caption.
options.risk: Calm can tip into museum-cold, and Etsy product photos with busy backgrounds will fight the flat field unless they sit inside white plates.

raised.raise: One module grid rules every alignment: plates, captions and the bento all snap to it.
Two inks only, celadon and jade-black; product photos are the only other colour.
Celadon is laid as a flat field that owns whole regions, never as a thin accent.
State is a mark, not a hue: in cart and favourited show as a stamped mark on the plate.

options.label: Red Envelope
options.lineage: hongbao red envelopes and New Year gold-foil packaging
options.thesis: The shop is a stack of red envelopes: vermilion fields, gold-foil edges, each product a gift of good fortune.
options.viewport: A vermilion field with the brand in gold, a centred line and new arrivals as gold-edged envelope windows with a gold Shop button.
options.risk: The most familiar direction for feng shui shops: it can read as Chinese New Year sale decor all year round.

options.label: Vermilion Fold
options.lineage: orizuru crane folded from vermilion washi
options.thesis: One sheet of vermilion paper folds the page into sections, crease lines dividing it and a gold dot marking where you are.
options.viewport: A vermilion sheet with diagonal creases, a folded square framing the newest arrival, and the serif line with a Shop button on the left.
options.case: Holds audience identification through auspicious red and gold, but folding is Japanese and says nothing about the products.
options.risk: Origami belongs to Japan, not feng shui, and the folds can bury the products.

options.label: Garden Guide Map
options.thesis: Sections as flat colour lobes on a map.
options.viewport: One green lobe swelling across the screen with capsule labels.
options.case: Theme-park energy loses on both audience and product clarity.

options.label: Dance Score
options.viewport: A centre staff with products as blocks.
options.case: No link to feng shui buyers and hard to shop.
options.kept: Strict symmetry as a layout law, considered but not needed.

options.label: Build Instructions
options.viewport: A numbered step with call-out boxes.
options.case: Toy assembly language misfits a spiritual home-goods shop.
options.kept: One module grid ruling every alignment.

options.label: Risograph
options.case: Zine culture is far from the audience, and fluoro inks clash with product photos.

options.label: Cutting Bench
options.thesis: A perforated rail of frames on orange.
options.viewport: A frame rail across a black and orange sheet.
options.case: Film-editing workflow means nothing to these shoppers.
options.kept: State shown as a mark, not a colour.

canonCard.label: The marketplace standard
canonCard.thesis: What Etsy-style shops ship: white page, search up top, a promo banner, then rows of product cards, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Logo and search bar, a soft banner, then a four-up product row.
canonCard.risk: Familiar to the client's Etsy buyers, and indistinguishable from every other shop by design.
